subject: MAP: hosting & region arbitration — MedSys close timeline
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@medsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: MAP: hosting & region arbitration — MedSys close timeline

Samir,

Attaching an updated MAP (v3) with a concise decision matrix for the deployment-mode + region choice based on the discovery notes last week. Key changes from v2:
- Added a pragmatic canary plan (hosted us-east) that keeps latency under 120ms for core workflows while we validate data residency needs.
- Clear lead-times: Hosted POC: 2–3 business days to slot; Dedicated staging -> prod: ~6–8 weeks (procurement + infra); Private (on‑prem/VPC): 10–14 weeks depending on networking approvals.
- Cost deltas included: Dedicated ~1.9x hosted list for provisioned capacity at steady state; Private varies—depends on infra ops assumptions.

Open asks for MedSys to confirm:
1) Are you comfortable starting POC on hosted in us-east for functional validation?
2) Do you require private-only for PHI workloads or only for production SLA coverage?
3) Any timing constraints for procurement that would force skipping Dedicated (e.g., Q3 production deadline)?

Attachments: MedSys_MAP_v3.xlsx, SOC2_report_2026Q1.pdf

If it helps, Laura can run a short session tomorrow to walk engineers through the canary plan and the Dedicated capacity estimate.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@medsys.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: hosting & region arbitration — MedSys close timeline

Rishi,

Thanks for the update and the matrix — useful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the MAP: 

1) Data residency: For the initial POC we can tolerate hosted in us-east (non-prod data). For production we need PHI to be kept within our VPC or in a redwood-managed Dedicated pool that ensures no cross-tenant KV sharing. Is that covered in the Dedicated model you outlined?

2) SLA and credits: Procurement will need a 99.9% SLA with credit schedule for sustained outages. Can you confirm whether that is standard for Dedicated customers?

3) Timeline pressure: We have an internal milestone on 2026-09-20 to start a controlled pilot. If Dedicated procurement is 6–8 weeks, we can still make that if we start procurement by mid-July — want to confirm gating items.

Cc'ing our contracts team for DPA / audit window questions.

- Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform, MedSys Health
samir.g@medsys.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@medsys.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: hosting & region arbitration — MedSys close timeline

Hi Samir — quick breakdown to address the three points. Long-form estimate attached (dedicated_capacity_estimate.xlsx).

- Data residency / isolation:
  * Dedicated: provisioned GPU pool with tenant isolation and encryption at rest (customer-managed KMS available). No shared KV by default; we've added a contractual clause in our Dedicated SOW template guaranteeing isolation semantics.
  * Private (VPC/on‑prem): full control over networking and storage; KMS within your boundary. Lead-time higher due to on‑prem validation.
  * Hosted: multi-tenant with logical isolation; not recommended for PHI-sensitive production workloads. Fine for POC if you limit dataset to synthetic or anonymized records.

- SLA & credits:
  * Dedicated customers can get 99.9% SLA in our enterprise contracts. Credit schedule: sliding scale with a 4‑hour detection window and pro-rata credits for minutes below target. We can surface the exact SLI/SDR language early in the procurement packet.

- Timelines & gating:
  * If procurement kickoff is mid‑July, Dedicated prod by 20‑Sep is achievable if legal, procurement, and security signoffs track to a two‑week review cadence. Recommended path: start procurement + security questionnaire this week, run hosted POC (us-east) in parallel to reduce risk.

Recommended next steps (proposed dates):
  1) Tue 07/06 — Solutions deep‑dive (45min) with your infra & security teams (we'll demo canary plan).
  2) Wed 07/14 — Procurement packet & Dedicated estimate delivered (Laura).
  3) Wed 07/21 — Security questionnaire complete / DPA draft reviewed.
  4) Mon 08/03 — Dedicated capacity reserved for staging (depends on signed SOW + payment).

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_estimate.xlsx

If that cadence works, Rishi will open the DocuSign for the SOW and I’ll circulate the Dedicated cost sheet.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MAP: hosting & region arbitration — MedSys close timeline

Laura / Rishi,

Thanks — before procurement packet is finalized we need the following captured in writing: 
1) Data Processing Agreement (DPA) covering PHI as defined under our BAAs — please provide a template or confirm Redwood's standard DPA is compatible.
2) Audit window: ability to receive SOC2 evidence and a 30‑day log retention snapshot on request.
3) Escalation path and contact details for production incidents; requirement that SLA credits are automatic and auditable.

Also note: our legal team will require a 30‑day review for any SOW that includes Dedicated or Private deployment (security review may add time). Please confirm you can accommodate that window and still meet the proposed pilot milestone on 2026‑09‑20.

Regards,
MedSys Contracts Team
contracts@medsys.com

Samir / Contracts team — thanks for the quick responses. Short plan to keep momentum: 

1) We will run hosted POC in us-east starting 07/07 (slot booked) — no PHI in the dataset, synthetic records only. Objective: functional validation and latency profiling (target <120ms median).
2) Laura to deliver Dedicated estimate and SOW draft by 07/14. We will include the Dedicated isolation clause and standard DPA language; SOC2 evidence attached to the procurement packet (SOC2_report_2026Q1.pdf).
3) Legal: we acknowledge the 30‑day review for SOWs including Dedicated/Private. To stay on the 09/20 pilot date we recommend parallel review (procurement + security) and a one‑page summary of the SOW for faster approvals — I'll route that today.

I will open the DocuSign for the SOW (link below) once Laura confirms numbers. Proposed immediate asks from MedSys: confirm the hosted POC start (07/07) and approve the list of security reviewers (name + email) so Laura can schedule the deep‑dive on 07/06.
